channel.title: Pysano Updates
channel.description: Stable and beta updates for Pysano.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.35
item.description:
# Pysano 0.8.0-beta.35
Experimental beta: not notarized by Apple.
- Choose Gemini, Qwen, Gemma, or Lapa for saved and freeform voice actions. Translate, summarize, rewrite, or ask a question about selected text. Local processing uses the same model downloads as Meeting notes. Choose a local dictation model as well to keep the voice instruction on the Mac. - Dictation sound options include macOS System, Typewriter, Gaming Keyboard, Toggle Switch, Wood Tap, Mellow Tap, and Water Drop. Preview the start and stop cues separately in Dictation settings.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.34
item.description:
# Pysano 0.8.0-beta.34
Experimental beta: not notarized by Apple.
- The dictation indicator fades into view and shows a dot pattern that reacts to your voice. A separate animation shows transcription, and distinct icons mark success and errors. - Bloom and Soft Click add two new pairs of recording cues. Preview each start and stop sound separately in Dictation → Indicator and sounds. - Since Beta 28, Pysano has gained more local speech models, improved long meeting summaries, and separate microphone and app audio tracks for meeting notes. When capturing app audio, the microphone starts off and the dictation shortcut toggles it during the recording.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.28
item.description:
# Pysano 0.8.0-beta.28
Build 42. Experimental beta: not notarized by Apple.
The app retains the established local code-signing certificate and Sparkle EdDSA key for beta updates. It has no Developer ID signature or Apple notarization. First installation on another Mac may be blocked by Gatekeeper. This release does not require changing system security settings.
- New notes workspace with a searchable recording library, summary/transcript tabs, source navigation and compact-window layout. The previous layout remains available. - Notes use the selected app palette, including Refined light/dark colors. - Separate transcription and summary model selection. Replacement transcription is checkpointed without erasing the previous readable result. Previous results are backed up before replacement; explicit summary regeneration uses a fresh cache identity. - More resilient insertion when an editor recreates its accessibility object. A replacement must match the original window, unchanged input context and editor anchor. - Prefer the app’s native Paste menu. Use private keyboard events addressed to the target process when no menu action is available. Stale global modifier flags no longer veto delivery. - Never automatically repeat an ambiguous paste. Unconfirmed text has separate private recovery copies under Latest text, so subsequent dictation does not overwrite it. - Key unlock is read-only and caches the key for the session. It no longer immediately requests an ACL rewrite. Key operations require a persistent app signature; packaging rejects ad-hoc signing.
The package uses the established signing identity. macOS owns the Allow/Always Allow decision; passwords are entered only in the system dialog. No Keychain permissions are weakened.
## Verification
120 automated checks, 761 localized strings, 19 distribution guards and five prepared-release guards passed. Native insertion checks covered 24 consecutive insertions, UTF-16 selection, recreated editors, rejection of a different destination, targeted keyboard delivery and a delayed paste without duplication. Ten native UI renders covered both palettes and model options.
Insertion checks used a synthetic editor. Live dictation into Codex and broad third-party editor acceptance still require real-world verification. AI summaries remain drafts that should be checked against their source quotes.

# Pysano 0.7.1
- The **Repair Key Access** action now rebuilds the legacy Keychain item's ACL once for Pysano's stable code signature, preventing an unlock prompt on every launch. - The API key remains in Keychain; there are no automatic system prompts and the key is never saved to project files. - Added four feedback sound sets: Liquid, Soft Chime, Pulse, and macOS System. - Liquid is the new default short cue. Every option can be previewed in Settings without starting a recording, and sound feedback can still be disabled completely.

# Pysano 0.7.0
- Made the dictation indicator smaller and moved its default position to the top so it does not cover the input field. - Added top, bottom, left, and right indicator placement options. - The completion message can be hidden or displayed for 0.5, 1, 2, or 4 seconds; the default is 1 second. - Added native macOS sounds at recording start and completion, with a separate sound toggle.

# Pysano 0.6.2
- Added a focused-node fallback for ChatGPT, Codex, and other Chromium/Electron/WebKit editors that expose `AXGroup` or `AXWebArea` instead of a standard text AX role. - Before insertion, Pysano revalidates the original app, window, and Accessibility node; password and secure containers remain blocked. - A missing Accessibility permission is no longer masked by an unknown text-field message. - After a failed attempt, the menu offers sanitized focus diagnostics that exclude field text, selection, keystrokes, and clipboard contents.
